metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract pessimism bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1.5–2% above immediate prior high.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 38.0) after a high, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.8% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to neutral/positive (e.g., +0.3 or higher), model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If model forecast is consistently 0.5–1.0% below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply “reversion bias” — add 0.2–0.5% to forecast for next 3 days to align with observed mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., +1.5% avg over last 5 days), model often underestimates; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast for next 5 days to capture momentum.
